chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami' al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi, from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar, from Aban ibn Taghlub, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas. He said: I heard the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, say:

The seekers of this knowledge are of three types. Behold, recognize them by their qualities and their signs. One group among them learns for argumentation and disputation, one group among them learns for stonewalling and deception, and one group among them learns for understanding and action. As for the one of argumentation and disputation, you see him causing harm and quarreling with men in gatherings of discourse. He garbs himself in humility yet is void of piety. So may Allah crush his chest and sever his nose. As for the one of stonewalling and deception, he dominates over his peers among his kind, yet humbles himself before the rich who are below them. He is a consumer of their sweets and a destroyer of his religion. So may Allah blind his sight and sever his trace from the legacy of the scholars. And as for the one of understanding and action, you see him possessing melancholy and grief. He stands in prayer during the darkness of the night, and he bows in his cloak. He works and fears, fearful and trembling before everyone except every trusted one among his brethren. So may Allah strengthen his foundations and grant him safety on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الِاسْتِطَالَةِ وَالْخَتْلِ: al-Istitalah wal-Khatl - Stonewalling and deception: using knowledge as a tool for social dominance and manipulation
key_terms.الْفِقْهِ وَالْعَمَلِ: al-Fiqh wal-'Amal - Understanding and action: the ideal pairing of deep comprehension with practical application of knowledge
key_terms.الْمِرَاءِ وَالْجَدَلِ: al-Mira' wal-Jadal - Argumentation and disputation: insincere debate aimed at showing off rather than discovering truth
key_terms.الْوَرَعِ: al-Wara' - Piety/scrupulousness: careful avoidance of anything doubtful or sinful, which the hypocritical scholars lack
key_terms.حَيْزُومَهُ: Hayzumah - Chest/sternum: used metaphorically in the invocation against the first type of knowledge seeker
key_terms.حِنْدِسِهِ: Hindisih - Its darkness: refers to the deep darkness of night during which the sincere scholar prays
key_terms.طَلَبَةُ: Talabah - Seekers/students: those who actively pursue religious knowledge, here classified by their varying intentions

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of knowledge seekers according to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, and how does he describe the characteristics of sincere versus insincere scholars?
ai.summary: In this famous teaching from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), transmitted through a ten-narrator chain via Ibn Abbas during a public assembly in 368 AH, the Commander of the Faithful classifies seekers of religious knowledge into three distinct types based on their underlying intentions: those who learn for argumentation, those who learn for domination and deception, and those who learn for genuine understanding and righteous action. For each type, he describes their characteristic behaviors and invokes a corresponding divine consequence -- destruction for the first, blindness for the second, and divine strengthening for the third. The teaching would have resonated with the scholarly circles of 4th-century Qum, where debates about sincere versus insincere scholarship were common.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Masrur narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Abdullah b. Ja`far b. Jami` al-Himyari narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. `Abd al-Jabbar from Abi Ahmad Muhammad b. Ziyad al-Azdi from Aban b. `Uthman al-Ahmar from Aban b. Taghlub from `Ikrama from Ibn `Abbas. He said: I heard Amir al-Mu’minin `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) say:

The seekers of knowledge are of three types. You can distinguish them from each other by their characteristics and signs. (1) One group are those who learn for insincere argumentation. (2) One group are those who learn for stonewalling and deception. (3) One group are those who learn for understanding and for acting by it. As for those of insincere argumentation, they bring harm and doubt to groups of men. They gown themselves in reverence, but they are void of piety. May Allah knock their chests and cut their noses. As for those who learn for stonewalling and deception, they obstruct those like them, and they humble themselves for the rich. Thus, they consume those for their sweetness, and they destroy their religion. May Allah blind them from their sight and sever their affect on the legacy of the scholars. As for the group who learn for understanding and for acting by it, they are seen melancholy and grieving. They stand in prayer in the darkness of the night, and they bow in their evening robes. They work [in good deeds], and they are cautious and afraid of everyone except their trusted brethren. May Allah strengthen their foundations and grant them safety on the Day of Resurrection.
